sn35.133:1.2: It is unusual, if not unique, to see a female brahmin with a student. Below she is referred to as the “tutor’s wife” (_ācariyabhariyā_). Since the tutor is absent, perhaps she is his widow, who took on the role of teacher with his passing. At Chāndogya Upaniṣad 4.10 we see the tutor’s wife (_ācāryajāyā_) discussing the education of the pupil. | Verahaccāni is not an attested clan name. Sanskrit _vairahatya_ means “manslaughter”; given that her husband is rather mysteriously absent, perhaps _verahaccāni_ is a term for brahmin ladies whose husbands were murdered.
